name: RPG Buildcraft Loop
description: A reusable character-build loop: experience grants skill and attribute growth; ranked nodes publish passive bonuses and unlock active abilities; Ability Loadout assigns actives to Hotbar; a confirmed Build Respec transaction refunds and resets selected build state without orphaned dependencies; completed changes trigger persistence. Currency pricing and respec planning are synchronous calls, not event round trips. Classes, content, UI, and exact balance tables remain host supplied.

components.role: experience, thresholds, and level-up growth events
ranked skill purchases, prerequisites, exclusive branches, passive bonuses, and skill respec plans
attribute allocation, derived stats, checks, and attribute respec plans
unlocked-active assignment, named presets, and stale-slot pruning
confirmed pricing, dependency-safe transaction orchestration, and exactly-once completion
synchronous respec affordability check and payment
loadout-bound cast execution, cooldowns, resources, and hit emission
single final-damage pipeline for selected active abilities
timed effects emitted by the same selected-ability hit stream

connections.note: Level growth grants the points and level gates used by ranked purchases.
The same growth event grants attribute allocation allowance.
Rank gains expose newly eligible actives and rank losses prune stale ones.
A completed skill reset removes actives whose source ranks disappeared.
The skill owner acknowledges its transaction id and actual skill-point refund.
The attribute owner independently acknowledges its part of the same transaction.
Only the skill tree mutates skill ranks after the confirmed plan is paid.
Only the attribute sheet mutates allocations and returns attribute points.
One complete snapshot replaces the executable kit; stale manual abilities cannot survive.
Selected actives use the ordinary final-damage owner.
Selected actives use the ordinary status ledger.
Successful rank changes are saveable; rejected purchases emit no state-change trigger.
Completed assignments and pruning are persisted.
Only a fully acknowledged respec transaction triggers its completion save.

acceptanceCriteria: A legacy tree node with no maxRank, costByRank, prerequisites, or exclusiveGroup behaves as a one-rank, one-point unlock with its original effect and restore behavior.
A new rank purchase succeeds only when level, prerequisite ranks, exclusive-group rules, maximum rank, and exact point cost all pass; rejection spends nothing and emits no rank-change event.
Passive bonuses are recomputed from current ranks and each node's per-rank effect, so rank gains, rank losses, restore, and replay cannot double-apply modifiers.
initialUnlocked and initialRanks restore prior builds without revalidating edited content, while every new purchase validates against the current tree.
Ability Loadout accepts only catalog actives whose source node meets minRank and whose slot, duplicate, and preset rules pass; an invalid preset applies no partial assignment.

A rank loss or completed skill respec prunes newly ineligible actives, publishes one complete loadout, and causes loadoutOnly Hotbar to reject casts from removed abilities without moving cooldown ownership.
A partial respec either rejects a plan that would orphan dependents or explicitly includes every dependent under cascadeDependents; the confirmed plan hash covers all affected ranks and refunds.
Build Respec calls economy.currency.spend synchronously after confirmation; insufficient funds reject before skill, attribute, loadout, or save state changes.
Each respec transaction id completes only after every expected skill and attribute acknowledgement arrives exactly once, and duplicate requests or acknowledgements cannot grant another refund.
A full respec resets the selected build scopes, returns skillPoints and attributePoints separately according to refundFraction, and leaves unspent-point ownership with the respective component.
Hotbar and Ability Loadout never apply passive skill bonuses directly; combat and movement owners read the published named modifiers and retain their own calculations.
Rejected purchases, invalid presets, and rejected respecs emit no completed-change save trigger, while successful rank, loadout, and respec changes do.
Removing Build Respec leaves level growth, ranked purchases, and loadout selection functional; removing Hotbar and combat resolution leaves a valid headless build-planning loop.
Identical restored state, tree content, timed inputs, and transaction ids reproduce ranks, bonuses, loadouts, prices, acknowledgements, and refunds deterministically.
